newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco cuts rates on T-bond issues 0.5 pt - Ministry.
newsitem.headline: Morocco cuts rates on T-bond issues 0.5 pt - Ministry.

text.p: Morocco has cut by half a point to between 8.5 percent and 9.5 percent interest rates on short and medium public Treasury bond issues, an official at the finance ministry said on Tuesday.

"To give impetus to the money market, we took the decision to cut by half a point (0.50 percent) interest rates on short and medium term public T-bond issues (emprunts nationaux)," the official told Reuters.

The monetary authorities reduced to 8.5 percent the interest rate on 52-week Treasury bonds, to 9.0 percent on three-year T-bond issue and to 9.5 percent on five-year Treasury bonds, the official added.
Public Treasury bonds are listed on the Casablanca bourse, the ministry said.
"The move aimed at encouraging competition on the market and helping medium seized enterprises to raise funds on the stock exchange," it said.
Subscriptions are open from 24 to 28 March 1997, it said.

The bonds divided in tranches of 5,000 dirhams ($532) and 50,000 dirhams ($5,319) are open to the public and all operators including foreign institutions to stimulate the bond market, the ministry added.

In the past, institutional investors were barred from access to public treasury bond issues, including insurance companies. But since September 1996, institutional investors have been allowed to subscribe to these bonds, officials said.
The government issues every three months public T-bonds and it was the second time it cut interest rates by 0.50 percent in a period of six months, a Casablanca-based market analyst said.
The government move coincided with Morocco's commercial banks to cut interest rates by two points on medium and long term investment loans to small and medium-sized firms, a banker said.
The Casablanca-based GPBM bankers' association earlier said the rate reduction decision was effective from March 1 to December 1997 "to contribute significantly to the country's economic relaunch."
King Hassan urged banks and the finance ministry, in his throne speech on March 3, to cut interest rates on loans particularly to small and medium-sized firms.
Total domestic borrowing more than doubled in 1995 to 13 billion dirhams from 5.2 billion dirhams in 1994, Bank al-Maghrib central bank said in its latest report.
Unofficial estimates put at 19 billion dirhams the total amount of the Treasury bonds issues in 1996.
